title: Mixed embeddings + chat: latency vs cost marginality sketch
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch of a mixed-workload benchmark we ran to surface marginal cost of small latency improvements when traffic mixes embeddings (short, CPU-bound requests) and chat generation (longer, GPU-bound requests). The goal is to produce collateral for sales/SEs showing where ops knobs buy the most cost savings versus latency regressions for realistic product mixes.

Test summary (synthetic but workload-oriented):
- Workload mix: 60% embeddings calls (avg tokens: 16, median latency small), 40% chat generation calls (avg prompt+response tokens: 240).
- Models/variants: open-embed-1 (CPU optimized), gen-7b-fp16, gen-7b-int8 (quantized), gen-13b-fp16 (baseline heavy).
- Hardware profiles: small-GPU (1xA10-like), mid-GPU (1xA100S analog), cpu-heavy (8 vCPU node).
- Batching policy variants: no-batching, opportunistic-windowing(20ms), session-aware-prefetch (prefix KV caching + tiny batch).
- Measurement window: steady 30-min runs, synthetic arrival process approximating Poisson bursts (mean rps 120, spike to 3x for 90s every 10 minutes).

Key takeaways (top-level):
1) Marginal cost for shaving p95 latency in mixed workloads is dominated by chat tail behavior; embeddings latency improvements are cheap but move the needle on cost-per-op less.
2) Small batching windows (10-30ms) provide >20% cost savings for gen-7b-int8 with <5% p95 regression under steady load; but under bursty arrivals p99 worsens significantly without prewarm slots.
3) Prefix/KV caching for chat sessions reduces amortized token work by ~12% across runs (best for repeated-turn conversational flows) and reduces observed p50/p90 cost-per-query.
4) For embeddings-heavy product usage (>=70% embeddings), favor CPU-optimized hosting + autoscale policies; cost curve is near-linear with concurrency but latency is stable.

Representative numbers (compact ASCII tables):
-- Average cost per 1k requests (USD) --
Scenario                        | 1k reqs cost
--------------------------------|-----------
Embeddings only (cpu nodes)     | $0.95
Mixed (60E/40C) no-batch        | $3.40
Mixed (60E/40C) 20ms window     | $2.72
Mixed (60E/40C) 20ms + KV cache | $2.40
Chat-heavy (40E/60C) baseline   | $4.90
Chat-heavy (40E/60C) int8+20ms  | $3.75

-- Latency percentiles (ms), Mixed 60E/40C on mid-GPU --
Variant                | p50  | p90  | p95  | p99
-----------------------|------|------|------|-----
no-batch (fp16)        | 85   | 230  | 310  | 540
20ms-window (fp16)     | 102  | 250  | 340  | 760
20ms-window (int8)     | 120  | 270  | 360  | 880
20ms+KV-cache (int8)   | 95   | 210  | 285  | 540

Notes about the numbers:
- p99 suffers most under bursty arrivals when batching windows cause queuing + the system runs out of prewarmed slots. The KV-cache mitigates this by reducing token generation for repeated prefixes.
- Cost-per-1k modeled includes GPU amortized per-minute slot price + token compute estimate + small I/O egress for embeddings (real S3 egress excluded). Not an invoice.

Micro-insights (operational knobs):
- Batching window trade: choose 10-30ms for mixed workloads if you care about cost; above ~50ms the p99 is unacceptable for interactive SLAs.
- Quantize aggressively for chat workloads that are tolerant of slight quality drop; int8 + minimal kernel-fusion gave ~22–28% cost savings versus fp16 at nearly identical p50/p90.
- Run embeddings on CPU pools with autoscale burst-backfill to avoid wasting GPU slots; embeddings are tiny but numerous and cause fragmentation if placed on GPU.
- Implement a small pool of dedicated prewarmed slots for handling burst spikes — amortized cost is small versus p99 penalties.

Visual vignette (sparklines encoded as token-lists to approximate charts):
- Cost vs batching window (USD per 1k): [no-batch:3.4, 5ms:3.1, 10ms:2.9, 20ms:2.72, 50ms:2.5, 100ms:2.4]
- p99 latency vs batching window (ms): [no-batch:540, 5ms:610, 10ms:700, 20ms:880, 50ms:1400, 100ms:2200]
- Fraction of cost from chat tokens (mixed workload): [chat_tokens:72%, embed_tokens:28%]

Questions / open work items: 
- Re-run with real client traffic trace (SE funnel) — synthetic Poisson approximates but doesn't capture correlated-turns in session. (JIRA: OBS-874)
- Add quality regression checks for int8 vs fp16 on a small eval set; quantify delta-LMScore on 500 samples.
- Explore hybrid scheduling: route embeddings synchronously to CPU nodes and route chat with opportunistic batching to GPU with a shared admission controller.

Actionable recommendations (for collateral):
- One-pager for SEs: "If your product mixes embeddings and chat, prioritize CPU pools for embeddings, enable 10-30ms batching on chat, and add KV caching for conversational apps. Expect ~20–30% lower cost for modest latency tradeoffs."
- Demo script: show cost-per-1k drop when enabling 20ms batching + int8, then show p99 spike during simultaneous burst and mitigation with 8 prewarm slots.
- Dashboard slices to add: cost-by-route (embed vs gen), p99-by-burst-state, prewarm-utilization over time.

Appendix (short methodologies & knobs we toggled):
- Arrival generator: poisson baseline with 3x spikes, concurrency targets to stress GPU queueing.
- Measurement: tokenized cost model + wallclock lat percentiles per request, 95% bootstrap CI for cost estimates.
- Infrastructure: k8s-like scheduler with slot-based GPU pricing emulated; embeddings routed via CPU autoscaler group.

Raw artifact pointers: JIRA-OBS-874 (bench harness), GH:infra/benchmarks/pull/57 (repro scripts), confluence: /display/OBS/embed-chat-2026 (in-progress writeup).

Notes-to-self: convert key tables to slide-friendly pngs, create simplified two-row table for sales handout ("what to enable" vs "expected savings"), and schedule a sync with SEs on 2026-03-18. 

----

This draft is intentionally concise and sloppier than final collateral — trying to capture interesting marginality and practical knobs rather than polished narrative.
